reviews.title: Heading south
reviews.text:
The Athletic 1.0 was great. Every club in the PL was covered, some great analytical articles, no adverts and not constrained by editorial word count so plenty of deep dives. 

Unfortunately it lost money. The current variant has sold its soul as the owners chase clicks.

Too many banal puff pieces on the big clubs who have multiple dedicated reporters, a significant number of PL clubs who have no reporters, force feeding of sports in which I have no interest, an initial few articles replaced by a Retch plc swarm of them, and now getting into bed with big tobacco. 

I get it, money matters and the owners priority is to shareholders, but it’s a coin toss whether or not to renew the subscription. 

Only thing making me want to potentially stay is the quality of writing from the likes of Slater, Crafton, Buckingham and Weatherspoon.

reviews.title: It’s changed since the NY times bought it
reviews.text:
1. You can feel the app repositioning towards maximizing your time on it. Now instead of only having articles about my interests, it displays all the sports big headlines. It used to be geared to what I wanted exactly. Now it’s a soup of interests and I have to click on my interests to navigate to that content. 
2. They got rid of several podcasts. One example of this is the Roundtable. The round table was different. Grant Bisbee and Company talked about baseball but also the perspective of covering baseball. Each week it felt like an ad hot conversation of three guys coming from the most inside perspective of baseball coming together and chatting about topics that truly informed and changed my opinion about ways to look at baseball. It was an incredible show – probably the best baseball show I’ve ever heard. Unceremoniously people had to ask in the comment session if it was happening this year. I believe it was Grant Brisby, who gave the notification from one of the hundred questions about the roundtable that came. I guess I don’t make enough money on Podcasts. Canceled.

It was a pretty great app and now it’s just fairly good.

reviews.title: What Happened?
reviews.text:
I have been a subscriber since the beginning, but I’m looking forward to my subscription ending. Once an excellent platform for football (soccer) fans, the NYT have completely destroyed any semblance of literate and informed journalism, preferring a populist circus, strewn with editorial errors and poor fact checking- all of which is blatantly censored to fit the NYT’s questionable political agenda.
The best writers have long gone. In their place, a bunch of sycophantic halfwits carry out the NYT’s objectives. The once well-rounded and broad podcast content is watered-down nonsense and the comments sections- once a forum where the writers would interact with readers- are ugly echo chambers where idiots are free to push their own hateful political narratives.
I would not recommend The Athletic to anyone even if it were free.

reviews.title: Control over notifications is significantly lacking
reviews.text: For many years, I've been able to configure push notifications in-app to suit my preferences perfectly. I set up notifications for the teams, sports and leagues that I enjoy following, and disallowed all other notifications. Recently they started giving push notifications for the Pulse Newsletter; theres no way to turn these off in the app. The thing that pushed me to make this review is that I've been getting intermittent push notifications about the World Cup, again with no way in app to turn them off. I think it's unreasonable to force users into receiving worthless notifications in order for them to receive the notifications that are actually wanted. I'll probably turn off notifications altogether at this point, which may eventually lead to cancelling my subscription since I suspect I'll read fewer articles as a result.

reviews.title: Downhill in so many ways
reviews.text: Subscribed for many years. My feed is consistently full of MLB NBA nonsense - I don’t watch every sport. I watch my sports I pay to read articles about my sports. Filling the feed with ads, and nonsense from other sports is just annoying.

reviews.title: Good writing, bad app
reviews.text:
The football writing is great, however the ads are a constant annoyance considering it is a paid subscription. 

Additionally, my feed is becoming increasingly busy with American sports stories that I am not interested in. I only subscribe to football three football related topics but I get annoying NHL, NFL, NBA, etc. news stories and video content. 

I’ve had to turn off all notifications because again, although I don’t subscribe to other sports I was getting notifications about them too. The app doesn’t match the quality of the writing.

reviews.title: DISAPPOINTING
reviews.text: The reading experience is awful when using Apple's VoiceOver screenreader as the World Cup countdown timer is constantly read aloud after every line. If VoiceOver is turned off and the article's speak option is used, this doesn't happen. However, the inbuilt speak option is not really a good workaround since it offers no control over what is being read, ie it reads from start to end and doesn't allow portions to be skipped if desired. The constant speaking of the timer happens even when the timer is not visible on the screen. This is an easy fix and, if provided, will go some way to show that ratings are taken seriously.

reviews.title: Pulse Notifications

A total disregard to their reader base. Good football (soccer) content but let down by a terrible attitude towards customers’ right to consume what they want to. Very disappointed and cancelling my subscription now.

reviews.title: Rendering customizations uselsss
reviews.text:
I follow every MLB team and F1 and the feed was glorious. But now it’s like you don’t even care what I follow because I get football, tiger woods, March madness, wwe, and I have to scroll the entire page to get to Jayson Stark or any baseball news.  Give me back my preference focused feed!  You have the news headline box to tout other things but give me everything baseball or I might as else just read the baseball writers feed in bluesky and be done with you

It’s bad enough that you do not have the foresight to understand that having a local beat reporter is what made the athletic a must have app. But tons of MLB teams don’t have a beat reporter any more. And some teams have two.   no One has local sports coverage any more as local news is dying and you have the opportunity to fill that gap with local beat writers.  You have to profits, invest in the journalism like you did with the NYT. Why don’t you get that if you build local, people will come?

I want to root for you but you make it hard

reviews.title: Payment Confirmation Issues
reviews.text: I want to be very clear.. this is not a one star review for the actual product, this is mostly a petty review for my frustration over the past week, and I’ve had enough of it. Now, I was signed up for a yearly subscription and my last payment was March. Since then, I changed bank accounts, so last week the website and app started showing a banner telling me I need to change my payment information. All I’m genuinely trying to do is complain because I’m upset and I really do enjoy The Athletic and could legitimately give it a 5 Star review. I changed my payment information and yet the payment still hasn’t seemed to go through the banner is still on the screen. Now I know i could just ignore it and keep reading, but the banner is annoying and it’s annoying cause I did what it said and it still didn’t go away. If you are considering subscribing and wanna know if you should, you should, if you work for The New York Times, please fix this issue with my account. The payment should be updated and I’m tired of your website trying to tell me that it is not.

reviews.title: Twitter Article to App Failure
reviews.text:
*Update* it gets even worse. I was browsing in the app and clicked on a link for "today's news" which went to a site within the app that showed the list of articles. When I clicked on the article to read, instead of going back to the app with the article, it prompted me to login and use a web browser reader instead. Initially saw the article on Twitter, but the seamless interaction still doesn't exist there either. 

When I see an article on Twitter that is interesting, I click the link, and it opens in the Twitter app reader. I hit the limit and it asks for my subscription info - instead, I select to open in the app. However, the link directs to the App Store (on IOS) and does not go to the installed and up-to-date app on my phone. When I open the app from the App Store, it goes to the homepage rather than the article. Worse still, I have trouble finding the article in the app. 

It used to work where I could link straight to the article in the app from Twitter, but now it’s no good. Please fix this.

reviews.title: Pointless for football unless a supporter of a “big” club

reviews.title: Good app - cynical ad clicking
reviews.text: The app is great and so is the content. The thing that really lets it down is when scrolling through an article as I read, if I happen to scroll on an area of the screen where an ad is it opens. This is not simply default behaviour - the action is clearly a scroll and not a tap so I can only assume it’s been developed to capture it as a click for ad revenue. This interrupts the reading experience and irritates me to the point where I won’t be renewing my subscription.
